question: How much noise can the array take, and does the best known ethylene-selective material fix ethylene?

protocol.noise: relative to each sensor full scale, floor 10% of the relative level times the median full scale
protocol.breakdown_definition: noise at which a gas error reaches half of the no-sensor error (always guessing the development-set mean composition), interpolated in log noise

literature.finding: apparent ethylene/ethane selectivity exceeding 10,000: ethylene 2.5 mmol/g vs ethane 0.098 mmol/g at 298 K and 1 bar; apertures 3.2 x 4.5 and 3.8 x 3.8 A; no methane uptake number given (breakthrough enriches ethylene from a CH4/C2H4/C2H6/C3H8 mixture)
literature.source: R.-B. Lin et al., Nature Materials 17, 1128-1133 (2018)

literature.finding: IAST ethylene/ethane selectivity 27 to 125 (equimolar, 296 K); ethylene heat of adsorption over 100 kJ/mol at low loading
separates ethylene/ethane and propylene/propane mixtures at 318 K
literature.source: E. D. Bloch et al., Science 335, 1606-1610 (2012)

noise_literature.source: B. A. Day and C. E. Wilmer, Sensors 20, 924 (2020)
noise_literature.note: genetic-algorithm MOF array design; noise modeled as a standard deviation of 5% of the signal
